title: Pramipexole: non-ergot dopamine agonist - directly stimulates dopamine receptors
vignette: A 58-year-old man comes to the office due to 8 months of a slowly progressive resting tremor of the right hand, stiffness, and slowness of movement. Examination shows a pill-rolling tremor at rest, cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia, and reduced arm swing while walking. He is diagnosed with Parkinson disease. Because he is relatively young and his symptoms are mild, the physician prescribes pramipexole rather than levodopa as initial therapy. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of action of this medication?

clues.text: pill-rolling tremor at rest, cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia
clues.note: The classic triad of resting tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia = Parkinson disease from nigrostriatal dopamine deficiency.
In younger patients, non-ergot dopamine agonists are often started first to delay levodopa and its long-term motor complications (dyskinesias, on-off phenomenon).
Pramipexole is a NON-ERGOT dopamine agonist that DIRECTLY stimulates postsynaptic dopamine (D2/D3) receptors, independent of the patient's own dopamine synthesis.

whatMatters: Pramipexole (and ropinirole) are NON-ERGOT DOPAMINE AGONISTS: they bind and DIRECTLY STIMULATE postsynaptic dopamine (mainly D2/D3) receptors in the striatum, bypassing the degenerating nigral neurons. This does not require conversion or endogenous dopamine. Answer B.
strategy: Classify the drug by name: pramipexole/ropinirole = dopamine-receptor AGONISTS (direct receptor stimulation). Contrast with the other anti-Parkinson mechanisms so you can reject them: levodopa (converted to dopamine - increases synthesis), amantadine (increases dopamine release/reuptake block), selegiline/rasagiline (MAO-B inhibition), entacapone/tolcapone (COMT inhibition), benztropine (antimuscarinic). The trap (A) is picking a mechanism that raises the patient's own dopamine, but agonists act at the receptor directly.

options.text: Increases synthesis of dopamine from levodopa
Increases release of dopamine from nerve terminals

eliminations.label: Increases dopamine synthesis - that's levodopa
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: raising dopamine by supplying its precursor (levodopa, given with carbidopa). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: pramipexole is a receptor AGONIST - it does not increase dopamine synthesis or depend on endogenous dopamine; it acts directly at the receptor. ✅ Correct if: levodopa/carbidopa.

eliminations.label: Increases dopamine release - that's amantadine
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: promoting presynaptic dopamine release (and blocking reuptake) - amantadine. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: pramipexole works post-synaptically at the receptor, not by releasing stored dopamine. ✅ Correct if: amantadine (also NMDA antagonist).

eliminations.label: Inhibits COMT - that's entacapone/tolcapone
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: blocking peripheral (and central) breakdown of levodopa/dopamine by COMT to prolong levodopa's effect - entacapone, tolcapone. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: pramipexole is not a COMT inhibitor and is not an adjunct that extends levodopa. ✅ Correct if: entacapone/tolcapone.

eliminations.label: Inhibits MAO-B - that's selegiline/rasagiline
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: blocking MAO-B, the enzyme that degrades dopamine in the CNS - selegiline, rasagiline. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: pramipexole does not inhibit MAO-B; it directly activates dopamine receptors. ✅ Correct if: selegiline/rasagiline.

eliminations.label: Blocks muscarinic receptors - that's benztropine/trihexyphenidyl
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: central antimuscarinics that rebalance the striatal dopamine:acetylcholine ratio, mainly improving tremor - benztropine, trihexyphenidyl. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: pramipexole acts on dopamine receptors, not muscarinic receptors. ✅ Correct if: antimuscarinic (tremor-predominant, younger patients).

reasoning: Classic resting tremor + rigidity + bradykinesia = Parkinson disease
Pramipexole is named as the drug; it is a non-ergot dopamine agonist
Dopamine agonists bind and directly activate postsynaptic D2/D3 receptors
-> directly stimulates dopamine receptors; answer B
mechanism: Parkinson disease results from degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta, reducing dopaminergic input to the striatum. PRAMIPEXOLE (and ropinirole) are NON-ERGOT DOPAMINE AGONISTS that bind DIRECTLY to postsynaptic dopamine receptors - preferentially the D2/D3 family - in the striatum, mimicking dopamine and restoring dopaminergic signaling INDEPENDENTLY of the patient's own (failing) dopamine synthesis or the number of surviving nigral neurons. Because they act at the receptor and do not require enzymatic conversion, they are often used as INITIAL monotherapy in younger patients to DELAY levodopa and its long-term motor complications (dyskinesias, wearing-off/on-off phenomena). Notable adverse effects include somnolence/sudden sleep attacks, nausea, orthostatic hypotension, hallucinations, and IMPULSE-CONTROL disorders (pathologic gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping). The distractors map to the OTHER anti-Parkinson mechanisms: increasing synthesis (levodopa), increasing release/blocking reuptake (amantadine), inhibiting COMT (entacapone/tolcapone), inhibiting MAO-B (selegiline/rasagiline), and antimuscarinic action (benztropine/trihexyphenidyl).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Neuro/Pharm > Parkinson drugs: dopamine agonists (pramipexole, ropinirole - non-ergot) directly stimulate dopamine receptors; delay levodopa; ADRs include impulse-control disorders, somnolence, hallucinations.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Pramipexole = dopamine-receptor agonist -> directly stimulates dopamine (D2/D3) receptors.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on dopamine agonist, D2/D3 receptors, non-ergot, MAO-B, or COMT? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Synthesis = levodopa; release = amantadine; COMT = entacapone; MAO-B = selegiline; antimuscarinic = benztropine.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: pramipexole/ropinirole = non-ergot dopamine agonists (direct D2/D3 stimulation); watch for impulse-control disorders + sleep attacks.

memoryHook: Pramipexole 'presses the buttons' directly - it doesn't wait for the brain to make dopamine, it walks up and hits the dopamine receptors itself.
